bomb._note: the thrown Bomb: `spin` while it flies, `fuse` once it has landed and waits for its blast. bomb_idle.png is unused. Anchor = the centre of the ball, so the lit fuse rises above the projectile position.

explosion._note: the Bomb's detonation: a one-shot radial burst centred on the blast. `fireball` is the widest frame's fireball width in `scale` px; the renderer scales the frame so that width spans the blast diameter.

explosion_small._note: a Cluster Bomb bomblet's detonation: the small sibling of `explosion` from the same pack and the same 192 px grid -- rounder, four short spikes, two frames shorter. Same keys and the same `fireball` rule, so `_blit_burst` sizes it by the bomblet's own blast diameter; it is the *look* that is lighter, not the size.

grave_totem._note: The Grave Totem (assets journal, 'Grave Totem sprite -- wiring', 2026-09-12): one strip per action, cut from Fire_Totem_blue-Sheet.png by tools/asset_pipeline/cut_totem_sheets.py. appear once at spawn (no bolts until it ends), idle between bolts, attack once per bolt, disappear once over the last second of life (no bolts). Anchor = bottom-centre on the base ring, 12 px under the summon's centre so the body stands on its collider like the primitive did.

totem_bolt._note: The Grave Totem's bolt (assets journal, 'Grave Totem bolt -- rework', 2026-09-12): the blue row of proyectile.png, cut by tools/asset_pipeline/cut_totem_bolt_sheets.py. `orb` pulses at the bolt (frames 3 4 5 6 5 4 of the row); `burst` plays once where a hit lands (frames 6..11), through slam_fx.spawn_impact -- `content` is the ball's box, `anchor` its centre, `over_circle` sizes the burst against the bolt's 6 px collider.

totem_bolt_fire._note: The bolt's tail: fire.png recoloured blue by tools/asset_pipeline/recolour_totem_fire.py (the multiply tint cannot turn orange blue). Authored pointing up (heading_deg 270); projectiles/totem_bolt.py rotates it to trail the bolt.

element_fire._note: Fire's aura: a ring that grows flame tongues outward.

element_ice._note: Ice's aura: a crystal that forms, then opens into a diamond outline.

element_thunder._note: Thunder's aura: a radial spiked discharge. The pack's purple rows are a dark indigo, a mauve and a magenta that Frostburn already owns, so this is its neutral grey row remapped onto a ramp centred on the element's own #6C4AA3 by the cut script.

element_wind._note: Wind's aura: concentric rings turning. Slower than the others on purpose -- it is the only pick that rotates, and at 14 fps the rotation reads as a flicker.

element_freeze._note: The freeze status: a block of ice that forms and shatters. 40 frames at 27 fps is 1.48 s, near enough the freeze's own 1.5 s that the shatter lands on the thaw. Indexed per body rather than by the shared clock, because each enemy freezes on its own schedule.

reaction_frostburn._note: Frostburn: a violet sphere of motes, where fire and ice blend.

reaction_overload._note: Overload: a hexagonal detonation, the biggest of the six. Remapped across its own pair -- thunder's purple in the shadows, fire's orange in the core -- because one authored row is one colour and this reaction has to state both of its elements. Fire and thunder are nearly opposite hues, so the ramp's ends are pushed apart and its gamma is above 1; a gentler one produced no purple at all.

reaction_superconduct._note: Superconduct: an orbiting star coming apart, which is what a chain reads as. Remapped across its own pair -- thunder's purple in the shadows, ice's blue in the highlights -- for the same reason Overload is: one authored row is one colour and this reaction has two elements.

reaction_firewind._note: FireWind. The three wind reactions are one swirl in three colours on purpose: they are the same mechanic with different payloads.

reaction_icewind._note: IceWind: the swirl in ice's blue.

reaction_thunderwind._note: ThunderWind: the swirl in thunder's purple, remapped from the grey row like the aura.

hammer_impact_plain._note: The Hammer's slam: a radial star from the point of impact. Worn by an uninfused weapon. The strip is already trimmed to the art's own bounding box, so `content` is the whole frame -- it is here because `slam_fx.impact_size` reads it for the aspect and would otherwise draw a 63 x 59 splash as a square. `over_circle` is the quarter the splash overhangs the blow by, as the art it replaces did.
